\title{A physics-informed digital twin for tube-life-aware operation of industrial steam methane reformers under uncertainty}

\author[su]{Izbassar Orynbassar\corref{cor1}}
\ead{izok2004@gmail.com}
\ead[url]{https://orcid.org/0009-0002-4224-3249}
\author[sua]{\todo{Second author name}}
\ead{m.sisenbay@aogu.edu.kz}
\cortext[cor1]{Corresponding author.}
\address[su]{School of Information Studies, Syracuse University, Syracuse, NY, USA}
\address[sua]{Safi Utebayev Atyrau University of Oil and Gas, Atyrau, Kazakhstan}

\begin{abstract}
\textbf{Background.} Reformer tubes are the life-limiting component of a steam methane reformer, yet operating decisions are rarely
taken with a quantified life cost.
\textbf{Methods.} We couple a one-dimensional Xu--Froment tube model, a long-furnace model of a top-fired box furnace, a
Larson--Miller creep-life module and Gaussian-process surrogates with conformal prediction into a digital twin. The tube model is
verified against the Xu--Froment industrial case, the coupled model is calibrated on three published plant operating points with
leave-one-out cross-validation, and the twin is exercised through global sensitivity analysis, hourly annual scenarios,
multi-objective optimisation and Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation.
\textbf{Results.} Calibration reproduces outlet temperatures within \SI{4}{K} and wall temperatures within \SI{12}{K}. Firing
intensity, steam-to-carbon ratio and excess air explain \SI{82}{\percent} of the hot-spot temperature variance. Load-following
costs less than \SI{2}{\percent} extra life per kmol of hydrogen, whereas catalyst ageing under a constant methane-slip target
multiplies the life cost by \SxAgeSlip{} in four years. A Pareto knee delivers \kneeHtwo{}\,\% hydrogen at \kneeFuel{}\,\% fuel and
\kneeLife{} of the base life cost, and creep-curve scatter contributes \shareCreep{}\,\% of the life-prediction variance.
\textbf{Conclusions.} The twin ranks operating regimes robustly, but absolute lives require alloy-specific rupture data and a measured
flame-length response to load.
\end{abstract}

\begin{keyword}
steam methane reforming \sep digital twin \sep creep life \sep conformal prediction \sep multi-objective optimisation \sep uncertainty quantification
